criteria.criterion: Repo root: nearest ancestor of the -C dir (or cwd) containing `.vloop`, else nearest containing `.git`, else the start dir; all printed paths are root-relative with `/` separators on every OS.
criteria.evidence: internal/config/root.go Root() loops .vloop then .git then start; FilePath const uses '/'; root_test.go covers all three branches; cli root() uses -C or cwd

criteria.criterion: Keys in order language, model.plan, model.work, model.review, effort.plan, effort.work, effort.review with the brief's defaults and valid values; resolution env over file over default.
criteria.evidence: config.go Keys table and resolve() (default, then file, then env with VLOOP_ + upper-cased key, '.'→'_')

criteria.criterion: `config list` prints `<key>=<value> (<source>)` per key, unset effort as `effort.plan= (default)`; `--json` is an object in key order of `{value, source}` with unset as null.
criteria.evidence: cli/config.go list uses Fprintf and writeOrdered to keep key order; jsonValue returns nil for unset; TestConfigListJSONOrderAndNull

criteria.criterion: `config get <key>` prints the value and a newline (empty line for unset effort); `--json` prints `{key, value, source}` in that order.
criteria.evidence: cli/config.go get: Fprintln, and a struct with fields in key/value/source order

criteria.criterion: `config set` validates, creates .vloop/config.toml under the root if absent, preserves every other key, prints nothing on success, leaves the file byte-for-byte unchanged when the value is already set, and `set <key> ''` removes the key.
criteria.evidence: config.Set: validate, no-op early return when the value is unchanged, MkdirAll and write, delete on ''; TestSetIdempotentByteForByte, TestSetPreservesOtherKeysAndRemoves

criteria.criterion: `config path` prints `.vloop/config.toml` whether or not it exists and creates nothing.
criteria.evidence: path command only prints config.FilePath; TestConfigPathCreatesNothing

criteria.criterion: Unknown key: `vloop: unknown config key "<key>"`, exit 2. Invalid value: `vloop: invalid value ... want one of ...` (models: `want a non-empty string`), exit 2, file untouched.
criteria.evidence: UnknownKeyError and InvalidValueError messages; Set validates before touching the file; TestConfigUsageErrorsExit2, TestRejectedSetLeavesFileUntouched; gate exercises these

criteria.criterion: An invalid value from the environment or the file, or a malformed TOML file, exits 1 with one `vloop: ` stderr line naming the source; under `--json` stdout still carries exactly one JSON document.
criteria.evidence: SourceError names the variable or FilePath; configErr writes a JSON error document under --json and returns Problem; TestConfigBadSourceExit1 and the gate

criteria.criterion: One TOML library is the only new dependency; nothing reads `~/.config` or any global path.
criteria.evidence: go.mod adds only BurntSushi/toml; no home or global path use in the code

criteria.criterion: Committed tests cover every key-table row, env/file/default resolution, idempotent set, removal, the exit-2 cases and all three root-resolution branches, in temporary directories.
criteria.evidence: config_test.go: TestDefaultsEveryRow, TestValidValuesEveryRow, TestEnvOverFileOverDefault, idempotent, removal; root_test.go has three tests; cli tests cover exit 2

criteria.criterion: No product code or test reads or writes this repo's `.loop/` or `.claude/`, or the home directory; tests work in `t.TempDir()` scratch repos.
criteria.evidence: grep of internal/ finds no .loop, .claude or home-directory access; the tests use t.TempDir()

criteria.criterion: `gofmt -l .` prints nothing, `go vet ./...` passes, and the module builds for linux, windows and the host.
criteria.evidence: gofmt -l printed nothing and go vet passed when I ran them; the gate log shows the tests passing; the driver ran the cross-builds as part of verify

notes: go.mod lists BurntSushi/toml as `// indirect` although it is imported directly. It is cosmetic, and `go mod tidy` would fix it. Set re-encodes the whole file, so comments in config.toml are not preserved; the brief only requires other keys to be preserved.
